title: When the Postcards Turns
premise: Rosalind Yarrow has spent twenty years tuning pianos and keeping her past in a locked drawer of sheet music — including the one song she co-wrote with her brother, who vanished the night their friend was killed. When a radio station plays that unrecorded song, credited to a dead man, she realizes someone has been living inside the story they buried. Returning to the fading mill town of Harrow Bend, she must confront the man who took the credit, the sister who helped her disappear, and the truth of what she traded her silence for. In the end, Rosalind chooses justice outside the law: she gives the song back to the town, testifies to what really happened, and lets the last postcard — the one she never sent — finally arrive.
about_author: Wendell Whitlock is the pen name of a former piano tuner who spent a decade restoring instruments in shuttered theaters across the American Midwest before turning to fiction. He writes about the debts people carry in their hands and the places that remember what they'd rather forget.

chapters.title: A Minor Repairs
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. In her quiet city practice, Rosalind tunes a dying upright and catalogs the unsaid things she keeps 'in inventory' — her brother's name, a town's name, a night twenty years old. The beat is controlled loneliness, a life built to avoid resonance.

chapters.title: The Song That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A car radio plays 'The Postcard Turn' — her song, her melody, credited to Ellis Marsh, a man officially dead since 2003. She nearly drives off the road. The beat is vertigo: the buried past has learned to broadcast.

chapters.title: Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, with letters from her brother Theo interspersed. She opens the locked drawer, rereads Theo's final postcard — never sent, addressed to the dead girl's mother — and decides to return to Harrow Bend. The beat is dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Harrow Bend, Tuning Down
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The mill town is half-abandoned; the Marsh house still stands. She takes a room above the diner and begins asking careful questions, learning that Ellis Marsh is alive, famous under another name, and coming home for a benefit concert. The beat is a town holding its breath.

chapters.title: What the Radiators Remember
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Tuning the Marsh family piano, she hears in the house's sounds the shape of the old night: three young musicians, one quarrel, one fall, one choice. A neighbor, Dovie, recognizes her and says too much. The beat is the past becoming physical, audible.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Kept the Door
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Rosalind and her estranged sister Maren, who stayed behind and married into the Marsh orbit. Maren reveals that Theo didn't run — he was driven out, and someone has been paying her hush money ever since, signed with a dead man's name. The beat is betrayal and reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Ellis, in the Flesh
chapters.summary: Ellis Marsh's POV. The famous man returns under his real name, rehearsing for the benefit, and knows instantly that Rosalind is in town. His chapters reveal the price he paid — and the lie he's been maintaining — to survive. The beat is a predator who believes himself a victim.

chapters.title: The Night, Retuned
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She reconstructs the true sequence: the girl, Lena, died in an accident Ellis caused; Theo took the blame's weight in exchange for their safety, then broke. Rosalind confronts Ellis in the Marsh house, and he offers her money, then threats. The beat is the climactic collision — truth against a fortress of lies.

chapters.title: Benefit Night
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. At the concert, Ellis performs 'The Postcard Turn' as his own; Rosalind walks onstage, sits at the second piano, and plays the song's true second voice — the part only she and Theo knew — forcing the town to hear the authorship. The beat is public reckoning, justice without handcuffs.

chapters.title: Return to Sender
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, coda. Ellis's world collapses quietly; Theo's fate is finally learned — alive, diminished, found through the song's broadcast. Rosalind mails the twenty-year-old postcard to Lena's mother, tunes the Marsh piano one last time, and leaves Harrow Bend lighter. The beat is grief transmuted into release.
